Living with Courage—What Harriet Tubman’s Life Teaches Us Now
Imagine this for a moment. You’re up against a tough decision—a parent worried about your kid’s future, an employee who knows standing up for fairness won’t be easy, or maybe a student questioning rules that just don’t feel right. Life can seem overwhelming, can’t it? The obstacles look huge, sometimes impossible to get past. But here’s what Harriet Tubman’s story reminds us: even the smallest act of courage, even a quiet moment of kindness, can send ripples further than you’d ever expect. Most of us don’t realize how much power we really have. We wait for someone else to step up, to fix what’s broken. But if you look at the Underground Railroad, the Civil War, every single chapter in Harriet’s life, you’ll see something clear—real change always starts with ordinary people who just refuse to back down. And the stories we tell about Harriet? They aren’t just about her. They’re about all of us. They nudge us to ask, “What would I do? Who could I help? What kind of world do I want to build?” The work isn’t finished—not by a long shot—but the path is still there, waiting for anyone who’s ready to walk it.
